segments.text: A cactus spine gives Gummy a sharp little poke.
But this cactus doesn't really have leaves.
Wide leaves are covered in tiny pores that leak water.
But deserts barely get any rain.
So the leaves shrank into thin, sharp spines.
Instead, the plump green stem handles photosynthesis and stores the water.
Look again - that spine used to be a leaf.
Spines are just leaves reshaped to save water.
